record.paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
record.original_question: Give criteria or proofs determining when the g.o. property of a homogeneous Riemannian metric is independent of the chosen coset representation M=G/K and of the chosen Ad(K)-invariant reductive decomposition g=k+m. Equivalently, clarify when the assertion that (M=G/K,g) is G-g.o. remains valid, changes, or must be reformulated after representing the same Riemannian manifold by another transitive isometry group or another reductive complement.

evidence.quote: does not depend on the representation

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold. A presentation of $(M,g)$ as a coset space is a pair $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively on $M$ by isometries of $g$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at a chosen base point, so that $M = G/K$. The pair $(G,K)$ is called reductive if there exists an $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant complement $\mathfrak{m}$ to the isotropy Lie algebra $\mathfrak{k}$ inside the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$, giving a decomposition $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ with $\operatorname{Ad}(K)\mathfrak{m}\subset \mathfrak{m}$. Such a complement $\mathfrak{m}$ is identified with the tangent space $T_oM$ at the origin.

The Riemannian manifold $(M=G/K, g)$ is called a $G$-geodesic orbit space ($G$-g.o.) if every geodesic of $g$ is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$; equivalently, for every $X \in \mathfrak{m}$ there exists $Z \in \mathfrak{k}$ such that $[X+Z,\, X]_{\mathfrak{m}} = 0$ with respect to some (hence any) $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive complement $\mathfrak{m}$.

Problem. Establish criteria, with proofs, that determine when the $G$-g.o. property of a homogeneous Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is independent of:

(a) the choice of $\operatorname{Ad}(K)$-invariant reductive complement $\mathfrak{m}$ in $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{k} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$ for a fixed presentation $M = G/K$; and

(b) the choice of transitive group of isometries, i.e., when passing from one presentation $(G,K)$ of $(M,g)$ to another presentation $(G',K')$ by a different transitive Lie group $G'$ of isometries of $(M,g)$.

In particular, clarify precisely under what hypotheses the assertion "$(M=G/K,g)$ is $G$-g.o." is invariant under change of reductive complement, when it transfers between distinct transitive isometry groups, and when (and how) it must be reformulated when the presentation changes.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on geodesic orbit (g.o.) manifolds notes that, for a fixed reductive presentation, the g.o. property is intrinsic to the presentation, but a general criterion describing how the $G$-g.o. property behaves under change of transitive isometry group or change of reductive complement is not stated as a settled theorem. Recent surveys and papers (2017–2025) on g.o. manifolds continue to discuss this issue and emphasize the dependence on the presentation, indicating the problem remains open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic orbit and weakly symmetric spray manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: For a reductive homogeneous space M=G/K with decomposition g=k+m, the spray vector field captures the geodesic orbit property; the dependence on the chosen reductive decomposition is discussed.
status_evidence.claim: The g.o. condition is typically formulated relative to a chosen reductive decomposition.

status_evidence.title: Geodesics in reductive homogeneous spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Reductive decompositions and their effect on geodesic descriptions are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Different reductive complements yield different connection-theoretic data, motivating the independence question.
